summary: an undeclared `setup` installs at the root of every tree the harness provisions, build worktrees included, and a consumer with no lockfile and no `setup` is refused at chain load
acceptance: one reduction answers how any tree the harness judges or builds in is provisioned, so an undeclared `setup` runs the engine's lockfile-aware installer at the root of a build worktree exactly as it does for the runner's base checkout; and a consumer whose tree carries no lockfile that installer reads while declaring no `setup` is refused at chain load naming the fix, rather than each tree failing late or resolving from the checkout above it
tests: a consumer declaring no setup gets the engine's installer at the root of a build worktree
a consumer with no lockfile and no declared setup is refused at chain load
pins: a consumer declaring a setup still provisions each directory it named

interface.changes: a consumer declaring no `setup` now has its build worktrees provisioned, and one declaring neither a `setup` nor a lockfile the installer reads is refused at load instead of at each tree
interface.hides: that the same undeclared `setup` meant an install for the runner's base checkout and no hook at all for a build worktree
interface.rejected: (b), a check refusing a worktree whose dependencies resolve from outside it — stack-specific (an upward walk is node's, prettier's, eslint's, each its own) and, with every tree installed, guarding nothing; it reopens if a consumer that declares `setup` is measured resolving from the parent

notes: Verified on this tip: the reduction answers the undeclared case with the engine's installer at the root while the worktree hook returns none, its doc arguing the engine must not install on its own authority — one question, two answers for one consumer. Field instance: no `setup`, so build worktrees had no `node_modules`, tools resolved the parent's, and a hook keyed on the worktree's own `node_modules/.bin` skipped silently. Operator ruling: option (a), with the no-lockfile arm made loud.
